name: Mug Nuadat

attributes.attribute: a name for a hero-king who ruled the south of Munster
fought a long war against Conn of the Hundred Battles
married Beare, the Spanish princess of a long peninsula
the founding name of the Eoganacht line

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mug Nuadat is an Irish name for a hero-king. The same man appears in the tales as Eógan, in his full form Eógan Mór. He ruled the south of Ireland, the province the tales call Munster. Old books make him the husband of the Spanish princess Beare, who gave her name to a long peninsula. In some accounts that princess hides an old goddess of the land. Eógan waged war without end against his rival Conn, the king who bore the name of the Hundred Battles. When Conn invaded his land, Eógan ran away to Spain. He came back to fight again. He was beaten again, and Conn killed him at last. His memory lived on as the founding name of the Eoganacht, the royal line that long ruled the south.
